_readme: Copy this file to data/cities/<your-city>.json and fill it in.
Then: pnpm plan --city <your-city>   (free, no API calls)
pnpm crawl --city <your-city> --dry-run   (shows the credit cost)
Only tiles and categories need real thought. Everything else is lookup.
TILES are the single most important part. The Google Maps engine caps a
query at ~200 results (page 11 returns zero), so no single query can cover
a city — you must tile it geographically. Measured overlap between two
Dubai tiles was ZERO, so tiles partition cleanly and are worth getting
right. Use real neighbourhood centres, not an even grid: business density
follows neighbourhoods, and an even grid wastes requests on water,
desert, and airports.
density controls pagination depth, so it is a direct cost lever:
dense   broad=5 pages, standard=3, niche=1   (city centre, commercial strips)
medium  broad=3, standard=2, niche=0         (residential with retail)
sparse  broad=1, standard=0, niche=0         (outskirts, industrial)
zoom: 15 for dense areas, 14 for medium, 13 for sparse. Higher = smaller area.
cityNames must match what the engine returns in the `city` field. Check a
single live result before crawling. City name is the primary filter and
bounding boxes are only a sanity check, because adjacent cities often form
one continuous urban area with a non-rectangular border.
Use several boundingBoxes if the city has detached territory.
